questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Italy, because i wanted to improve the level of italian i learned in high school. In Milan i could get courses that were similar to the ones i would have had at home and therefore i chose this as my destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It ws easy, most information was received by e-mail. However some informations were received a bit late.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: How to sign into classes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The host institution provided some rooms in a student housing. The campus housing were shared rooms and the rent was very cheap.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Big kitchens, kitchen tools however had to be brought from home or bought at the destination. The reception at the dorm also sold cheap kitchen kits.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's a good way to meet neww people and usually very cheap.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The informations on how to register came a bit late but it was easy to register when we got the information

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to enter the courses I wanted to attend, and were after that accepted to the courses. Later on we also had to register for the mid-terms and exams in the same platform.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A how-to guide was uploaded on the platform.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's easy when you follow the guide

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses that were 1.st year master degree courses. It was not to hard to follow as I am on my last year of the bachelor.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar but a lot more theoretical than practical. We had both group work, lectures, seminars and individual work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Agricultural Systems and Soil Science (6 ECTS )
Environmental Accounting and Management (12 ECTS)
Law of Territorial Government and Public Contracts (6 ECTS)
Natural Resource Economics (6 ECTS)
Additional Language Skills: Italian Level A2 (3 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would reccomend all of them, the professors and the material provided were good

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The housing was less expensive than i thought, it's also very cheap to go out to eat/have coffee compared to Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I only joined the Erasmus activities and not the university non-academic activities

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I donøt know

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining the Erasmus activities

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on trips e.g. to lago maggiore, como/bellagio, genova, cinque terre, bologna, parma...
Join some events that are organised by ESN or other Erasmus students

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy, there's a lot of exchange students at UNIMI so people are used to it.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The mindset on time. People are often late and informations also come later than you would expect.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food, history, art and most people are very kind and open

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get used to not always be able to plan everything in good time 

Join many ESN events to boost your social life 

Start studying early for the exam, i found that there was a lot to catch up on at the end of the semester

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's a lot of exchange students in the master courses at the university, therefore everyone is willing to/used to speak english

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I has been very rewarding both on social skills and academical skills. I can't say what was the most rewarding part.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: When i first arrived and had to get used to everything in a new city where i didnt really know anybody. It was nice to have a roomate who was also on exchange because we quickly became friends and could talk to each other about all the new things

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
